newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper editorials - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper editorials - July 23.

text.p: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The ECONOMIC TIMES said while the relationship between China and Taiwan could not go any further at the moment, Hong Kong should take a pragmatic approach when developing its relationship with Taiwan. It said despite government policies, most Taiwan businessmen did not want to give up investment opportunities on the mainland, and Hong Kong could act as a bridge between them and the mainland market.

-- The Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO said Hong Kong's labour shortage could be resolved if the government provided better training to laid-off workers and if employers were willing to hire new workers. Since the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government was concentrating on people's livelihood, this kind of problem could be easily solved, the paper said.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said the Department of Justice's refusal to pay for a senior counsel to lead the defence challenge to the validity of the provisional legislature was hardly an example of justice being seen to be done. It said that unless the question was resolved, the present uncertainty and prospect for legal challenges would remain.
